fields.subnational_unit: eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality (Durban), KwaZulu-Natal; Phoenix, Inanda, Tongaat and KwaXimba (wards 1, 3, 52, 54, 56, 57, 61; about 357,492 residents)
fields.population: community members who had registered water-availability complaints (from councillor databases) and municipal water-department staff
fields.sample_size: 40 participants in focus groups: five community members per community (Phoenix, Inanda, Tongaat, KwaXimba) and groups of five municipal water-department staff; interviews 30-60 minutes; transcripts analysed in NVivo
fields.effect_measure: inductive thematic analysis of community and municipal-official focus groups; cross-comparison of the two perspectives
fields.effect_estimate: Community themes: water-quality concerns; boreholes as preferred solution; allegations that water tankers and repairs favour supporters of governing parties; administrative inefficiency (estimated billing for no water, Tongaat residents owing over R60,000 and pushed onto payment plans; slow burst-pipe repairs); vandalism, sabotage and illegal connections. Official themes: ageing, overstretched infrastructure with missing asset records; non-revenue water as the central crisis (about 50% lost, over R2 billion a year to illegal connections, 120,000+ non-recording meters); rapid urbanisation and informal settlements outside formal addresses and planning frameworks (including Ingonyama Trust Board land). The authors frame scarcity as a multidimensional governance crisis. No effect estimate.
fields.model_type: qualitative thematic analysis (NVivo) of focus groups
fields.study_design: qualitative case study using focus-group discussions with community members and municipal officials (not a quantitative cross-sectional design)
fields.section: Full text (MDPI Urban Science): Abstract; Methods 3.1-3.8; Results 4.1-4.6
fields.exact_location: Abstract p1; sampling p7-8; community themes 4.1-4.5 p13-14 (4.3 political manipulation; 4.4 administrative inefficiency); official themes 4.6 p14-16

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative focus-group study (40 participants) of water scarcity and infrastructure in eThekwini Municipality, South Africa, read in full text 2026-10-04. Community accounts of politicised tanker allocation and estimated billing, and official accounts of non-revenue water, illegal connections and informal settlements outside planning frameworks. Qualitative design: the JBI cross-sectional tool applied earlier does not fit (reclassification candidate).
